title: TIPAngle: Traffic Tracking at City Scale by Pose Estimation of Pan and Tilt Intersection Cameras
problem: Pan-and-tilt traffic cameras often lack angle sensors or orientation feedback, making robust traffic tracking difficult. Deep learning approaches for camera pose estimation are compute-intensive and unsuitable for embedded deployment.
motivation: City-scale traffic monitoring with thousands of pan-and-tilt cameras requires efficient on-device pose estimation to determine camera orientation when sensors are unavailable or disabled, enabling reliable vehicle tracking across camera rotations.
method: A Siamese neural network (two identical networks that compare image pairs to detect differences) learns to estimate camera pan and tilt angles. The inference runs on Raspberry Pi's CPU at ~17 frames per second through optimization, avoiding the need for external hardware.
key_novelty: A Siamese network optimized for CPU enables real-time camera angle tracking on Raspberry Pi (17 Hz), achieving 18.45x faster inference and 3x better accuracy than ResNet-18.
contributions: Lightweight Siamese architecture for camera pose estimation
Real-time inference on Raspberry Pi CPU (57ms per frame, 17 Hz)
limitations: Evaluation focused on angle estimation accuracy and inference speed; full end-to-end tracking performance metrics not detailed. Limited to Raspberry Pi platform.
primary_theme: Lightweight neural networks for edge video analytics
